title: Crispy Skin Salmon
subtitle: Pan-fried salmon with capers, lemon, and parsley
excerpt: Crispy skin salmon is one of the fastest things you can cook well. The trick is a dry, cold skin, a hot pan, and patience: press the fillet flat and do not move it for the first few minutes. Capers and lemon in the pan become a simple sauce as the fish rests.
sourceNotes: Standard European pan-frying technique for fish, widely used in French and British restaurant kitchens. The key variables are dry skin and a very hot pan.

content.text: Pat the skin completely dry before cooking and do not move the fish once it hits the pan. The salmon will stick at first but release on its own when the skin is properly crisp.
Pat the salmon skin completely dry with kitchen paper. Season the skin side with salt. Heat the olive oil in a large frying pan over high heat until the oil is shimmering.

Place the salmon fillets skin-side down in the pan. Press each one flat with a spatula for the first 30 seconds to prevent curling. Cook for 4 to 5 minutes without moving, until the skin is deeply golden and crisp.
Flip the salmon. Cook for 1 to 2 minutes more depending on how well done you like it. Remove from the pan and rest on a warm plate.
Reduce the heat to medium. Add the capers to the pan and let them sizzle for 30 seconds. Squeeze in the lemon juice and add the parsley. Swirl and pour over the salmon. Serve with lemon wedges.

items.cause: Pan was not hot enough or skin was wet.
items.fix: Dry the skin well and get the pan very hot first.

items.cause: Moved too soon before the skin crisped.
items.fix: Do not move it. It will release cleanly when crisp.

items.cause: Too long on the flesh side.
items.fix: Reduce flesh-side cook to 1 minute for a moist centre.
